summary: The note surveys how blockchain startups are applying the technology beyond cryptocurrency, focusing on BlockLogix, a supply chain startup founded by Jennifer Chu and Marcus Quintanilla. It traces their path from idea validation and accelerator participation to pilot customers, partnerships and consortium membership, while covering hype versus reality, scalability, regulatory challenges and the setbacks faced by NSCoder.
one_line: Blockchain startups like BlockLogix and NSCoder apply the technology to supply chains and code validation beyond cryptocurrency, facing hype, scaling and regulatory hurdles.
key_facts: Satoshi Nakamoto released the Bitcoin whitepaper in October 2008, which planted the seed for blockchain technology extending beyond digital currency.
Blockchain is described as a decentralized ledger made of data blocks chained together in a public or private network, with each new transaction recorded in every participant's ledger.
Jennifer Chu, a supply chain veteran, and Marcus Quintanilla, a cybersecurity expert, co-founded BlockLogix to bring transparency and efficiency to the supply chain industry.
Chu was frustrated by the lack of transparency in supply chains she managed, while Quintanilla saw growing cyber-attack risks on centralized databases.
BlockLogix built a proof of concept and then a minimally viable product (MVP) offering a tamper-evident, immutable record of every item moving through the supply chain.
BlockLogix took part in startup accelerators such as the NextGen Entrepreneurship Program, which commenced on September 15, 2023.
Chip Wexler, a partner at venture capital firm Beacon Innovate, said on November 10, 2023 that blockchain 'is certainly transformative, but it is not a cure-all remedy.'
By December 2023, BlockLogix was implementing its solution with a select number of pilot customers, reporting fewer counterfeit goods and more efficient recall processes.
On January 14, 2024, BlockLogix announced a partnership with major logistics firm GlobalTrans to refine its model and scale.

The Blockchain for Greater Good Consortium, launched on February 20, 2024, brought startups including BlockLogix together to apply blockchain to public sector transparency and environmental monitoring.
The Blockchain Regulatory Advisory Body was formed on March 4, 2024 to help develop a stable legal framework for non-cryptocurrency blockchain applications.
NSCoder, a blockchain startup focused on secure code validation, faced setbacks integrating its solution with existing development workflows but carved out a niche through user-centric design.
NSCoder CEO Eva Tsai said in her CodeSecure Conference 2024 keynote: 'Every setback has sharpened us.'
Blockchain startups in healthcare focus on securing patient data, while in the art world they focus on certifying artwork provenance.
